generation_model.gap_discovered_by: Delegated investigation (Explore agent) scoped to normalization conflict-handling, census assembly, and non-Rust semantic extractors -- areas not yet audited this session. Independently verified the one real finding directly against the code: `adapter/src/semantic/rust/mod.rs:449,501,574,620,831` each call `debug_assert!(observation.is_dimension_consistent())` -- a no-op in release builds -- rather than a real, always-enforced check, unlike the equivalent invariant checks in test-side fixture builders (`runtime/src/census/mod.rs`, `runtime/src/census/extraction.rs`), which use plain `assert!`.

priority_classification: investigated, not actionable this generation -- would be priority 1 (correctness) if live, but is currently unreachable by construction (see design_decisions) and converting it to a real check without further care would introduce a new risk (see the specific reason below), so it does not meet the bar for a well-scoped fix right now.

design_decisions.question: Should `debug_assert!` simply become `assert!` (matching the test-side convention) so the invariant is enforced in release builds too?
design_decisions.decision: Not this generation. Verified directly: at each of the 5 call sites, the same local `dimension` variable seeds both `SemanticRecordId::new(dimension, ..)` (the header) and the immediately-following variant-constructor selection, so no code path today can actually produce a dimension-inconsistent observation -- the check is currently unreachable, not currently protective. Separately and more importantly, verified this codebase has NO panic-isolation boundary anywhere in production code (grepped the whole workspace for `catch_unwind`: zero results, in or out of test code). This extraction pipeline's own established resilience principle (`production_wiring_extracts_real_rust_semantics_and_isolates_a_malformed_file`: a read failure or parse failure on one artifact must never abort or erase the whole batch) means a bare `assert!` that DID fire (from some future refactor this generation cannot predict) would crash the entire `systemize`/census run for the whole repository, not just isolate the one problematic observation -- trading a currently-harmless no-op for a new, real availability risk, for a defect that cannot occur today. That is a worse outcome than the status quo, not a strict improvement, so it is not a safe drop-in fix. A correct fix would instead need to make dimension-inconsistency a diagnosed, isolated, skip-this-observation outcome (consistent with this session's own 'never fabricate, never crash the whole pipeline for one bad input' pattern already applied elsewhere), which requires restructuring each of the 5 call sites' control flow to a fallible path -- a meaningfully larger, more invasive change than the risk (currently zero, by construction) justifies right now.

overall_verdict: INVESTIGATED, ONE REAL FINDING DELIBERATELY DEFERRED WITH REASONING. The normalization/census/extractor area of this codebase is confirmed well-hardened (conflict-candidate non-resolution is documented contract behavior, not a silent drop; census assembly has no drop/double-count gap; the only real extractor's DoS guard already covers generic/nested-type recursion). The one real finding (debug_assert-only dimension-consistency checks in the Rust extractor) is currently unreachable by construction, and naively hardening it without first addressing the complete absence of panic isolation in this codebase would trade a harmless no-op for a new availability risk -- correctly deferred rather than fixed hastily.
